channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: ‘Lesser evil’ or ‘huge victory’? Analysts split on proposed US-China trade board ahead of Trump-Xi
item.description: US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to As trade disputes loom over this week’s meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, proposals for a “Board of Trade” and a separate “Board of Investment” may be on the table.

item.title: Sharp drop in ‘forever chemicals’ in seabird eggs hailed as win for regulation
item.description: PFAS levels in northern gannet eggs in Canada' Levels of Pfas in northern gannet eggs in Canada fell up to 74% over 55-year period of studyLevels of some of the most dangerous Pfas compounds have dramatically fallen in Canadian seabird eggs, which the authors of a new peer-reviewed study say illustrates how regulations are effective. item.title: Storm, displacement and hidden wartime explosives deepen emergency in Solomon Islands
item.description: Tropical Cyclone Lisa has affected over 150,000 people in the Solomon Islands. The storm has created significant humanitarian needs across the nation. Unexploded ordnance from World War II poses an additional threat to displaced populations. More than 150,000 people have been affected by Tropical Cyclone Maila, the latest storm in the Pacific area, which continues to drive what the UN relief coordination office OCHA has described as “significant humanitarian needs” across the Solomon Islands.

item.title: Armed drones leading cause of civilian death in Sudan war: UN rights chief
item.description: Armed drones caused over 80 percent of civilian deaths in Sudan during the Drones caused more than 80 per cent of civilian deaths in Sudan’s war during the first four months of 2026, killing at least 880 people, the UN human rights chief said on Monday, warning that escalating drone warfare could push the conflict into an even deadlier phase.

item.title: Strait of Hormuz de-escalation is urgent, says UN chief
item.description: The UN Secretary-General called for urgent de-escalation in the Strait As the Strait of Hormuz crisis deepens and tensions between Iran and the United States remain unresolved, oil prices rose again early Monday, prompting the UN Secretary-General to call for a peaceful resolution and warn of the widening fallout across Africa and beyond.

item.title: US and Mexico brace for heatwave as deadly floods hit South Africa
item.description: A heatwave is expected to intensify across the western United States and Mexico this Temperatures soar in California and Arizona, while deluge continues across Western and Northern CapeHeat is expected to intensify across western parts of the US and Mexico this week as a ridge of high pressure pushes temperatures well above the seasonal norm.

item.title: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope?
item.description: Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a summit with Chinese US leader enters talks with superpower rival from vulnerable position, but will be hoping for economic wins amid turbulent backdropIf all goes to plan over the next few days – and that is a big if – Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a highly anticipated summit with Xi Jinping, China’s leader. The trip will mark the first time a US president has visited China in nearly a decade.

item.title: Indonesian rescuers retrieve body from Mount Dukono as search continues
item.description: Indonesian rescuers recovered the body of a woman after a volcanic eruption on Mount Woman recovered after volcanic eruption on remote island, while operation to find two missing Singaporeans goes onRescuers have recovered the body of an Indonesian woman who was caught in a volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono on Indonesia’s remote island of Halmahera, officials have said. Search operations continued on Saturday for the bodies of two Singaporeans.

item.title: ‘Watching us is like watching a cousin’: the online creators reshaping Africa’s news ecosphere
item.description: Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa posted a TikTok video explaining a dispute between the South African and Rwandan presidents. She detailed the roles of various South African groups in a conflict. Jaxa's content focuses on current affairs for a South African audience. Africa is leading a change in news consumption habits – and transforming the lives of current affairs enthusiastsLast year Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa posted a TikTok video about South African peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

item.title: Guardian reporter and colleagues detained and beaten by Somali police
item.description: Guardian reporter Mohamed Bulbul was detained and beaten by Somali police in Mogadishu. He was arrested with two colleagues, Abdihafid Nor Barre and Abdishakur Mohamed Moh. The arrests followed Bulbul's reporting for the Guardian on the alleged torture of a woman in prison.

item.title: Central African Republic: Funding cuts put humanitarian support at risk
item.description: Funding cuts threaten humanitarian operations in the Central African Republic. The Central African Republic (CAR) is making progress towards stability and security but major aid budget cuts threaten humanitarian operations there, a senior official with the UN aid coordination office OCHA said on Friday in New York.

item.title: Three hikers dead after Indonesia’s Mount Dukono volcano erupts
item.description: Three hikers, two Singaporean and one Indonesian, died on Halmahera island after Mount Dukono erupted. They were in a restricted area when the volcano ejected an ash cloud approximately 10 kilometers high. No nearby villages were affected by the eruption.
